verses.1: And immediately in the morning the chief priests with the elders and scribes, and the whole council, held a consultation. They bound Jesus and led Him away and delivered Him to Pilate.
verses.2: And Pilate asked Him, "Are you the King of the Jews?" And He answered him, "You have said so."
verses.3: And the chief priests accused Him of many things.
verses.4: And Pilate asked Him again, saying, "Have you no answer? See how many charges they bring against you."
verses.5: But Jesus made no further answer, so that Pilate was amazed.
verses.6: Now at the feast he used to release for them one prisoner for whom they asked.
verses.7: And there was a man called Barabbas, imprisoned with the rebels who had committed murder during the uprising.
verses.8: And the crowd came up and began to ask Pilate to do as he usually did for them.
verses.9: And Pilate answered them, saying, "Do you want me to release for you the King of the Jews?"
verses.10: For he perceived that it was out of envy that the chief priests had delivered Him up.
verses.11: But the chief priests stirred up the crowd to have him release Barabbas for them instead.
verses.12: And Pilate again said to them, "Then what shall I do with the man you call the King of the Jews?"
verses.13: And they cried out again, "Crucify Him!"
verses.14: And Pilate said to them, "Why, what evil has He done?" But they cried out all the more, "Crucify Him!"
verses.15: So Pilate, wishing to satisfy the crowd, released Barabbas for them, and having flogged Jesus, he delivered Him to be crucified.
verses.16: And the soldiers led Him away inside the palace — that is, the Praetorium — and they called together the whole battalion.
verses.17: And they clothed Him in purple, and twisting together a crown of thorns, they put it on Him.
verses.18: And they began to salute Him, "Hail, King of the Jews!"
verses.19: And they were striking His head with a reed and spitting on Him, and kneeling down in mock worship before Him.
verses.20: And when they had mocked Him, they stripped Him of the purple and put His own garments on Him. And they led Him out to crucify Him.
verses.21: And they compelled a passerby, Simon of Cyrene, who was coming in from the country — the father of Alexander and Rufus — to carry His cross.
verses.22: And they brought Him to the place called Golgotha, which means Place of a Skull.
verses.23: And they offered Him wine mixed with myrrh, but He did not take it.
verses.24: And they crucified Him and divided His garments among them, casting lots for them to decide what each should take.
verses.25: And it was the third hour when they crucified Him.
verses.26: And the inscription of the charge against Him read: THE KING OF THE JEWS.
verses.27: And with Him they crucified two robbers, one on His right and one on His left.
verses.28: And the Scripture was fulfilled that says, "He was numbered with the transgressors."
verses.29: And those who passed by hurled insults at Him, shaking their heads and saying, "Ha! You who would destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days,
verses.30: save yourself and come down from the cross!"
verses.31: So also the chief priests with the scribes mocked Him among themselves, saying, "He saved others; He cannot save Himself.
verses.32: Let the Christ, the King of Israel, come down now from the cross that we may see and believe." And those who were crucified with Him also reviled Him.
verses.33: And when the sixth hour had come, there was darkness over the whole land until the ninth hour.
verses.34: And at the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice, "Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?" which means, "My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?"
verses.35: And some of the bystanders hearing it said, "Look, He is calling Elijah."
verses.36: And someone ran and filled a sponge with sour wine, put it on a reed and gave it to Him to drink, saying, "Wait, let us see whether Elijah will come to take Him down."
verses.37: And Jesus uttered a loud cry and breathed His last.
verses.38: And the curtain of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom.
verses.39: And when the centurion who stood facing Him saw that He breathed His last in this way, he said, "Truly this man was the Son of God!"
verses.40: There were also women watching from a distance, among whom were Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James the younger and of Joses, and Salome.
verses.41: These women had followed Him and ministered to Him when He was in Galilee, and there were also many other women who had come up with Him to Jerusalem.
verses.42: And when evening had come, since it was the day of Preparation — that is, the day before the Sabbath —
verses.43: Joseph of Arimathea, a respected member of the council who was also himself looking for the kingdom of God, took courage and went to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.
verses.44: Pilate was surprised that He had already died. And summoning the centurion, he asked him whether Jesus had been dead for some time.
verses.45: And when he learned from the centurion that He was dead, he granted the body to Joseph.
verses.46: And Joseph bought a linen shroud, and taking Him down, wrapped Him in the linen shroud and laid Him in a tomb that had been cut out of the rock. And he rolled a stone against the entrance of the tomb.
verses.47: Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses saw where He was laid.
